analogy.name: A single-chef restaurant
analogy.line: The event loop is like one chef: he cooks one dish at a time, orders wait on a ticket rail, and the ovens and timers work on their own while he moves on.

js-core.caption: JavaScript runs one thing at a time. Async work waits in a queue until the stack is empty, then the event loop lets it in.
steps: The chef's hands are the call stack. Real name: it runs your code one frame at a time. A long task here freezes the whole kitchen.
The ovens and timers are Web APIs. Real name: timers and fetch run outside JavaScript on their own clocks, so waiting costs the chef nothing.
The ticket rail is the callback queue. Real name: finished work lines up in the order it completed, waiting for the chef.
The chef glancing up is the event loop. Real name: when the stack is empty, take the next callback. That is the whole trick.

analogy.name: A proofreader's red pen
analogy.line: TypeScript is like a proofreader: he marks every problem on the draft, then the clean copy is printed without any of his marks. The printed page is plain JavaScript.

typescript.caption: TypeScript checks your types and then deletes them. The JavaScript that ships has no types in it at all.
steps: The draft is your source. Real name: code with annotations, or none, where the compiler infers types from how a value is used.
The proofreader reads for meaning. Real name: inference. A const string becomes that exact literal, not just string.
He marks each branch as proven. Real name: narrowing. After an if check, the type is smaller and the compiler knows it.
The clean copy is printed. Real name: emit. Types are erased, so nothing validates data at runtime unless you add a library like zod.

analogy.name: A restaurant host at the door
analogy.line: Node is like a single host who seats guests and takes orders but never cooks: slow jobs go to the kitchen, and he only handles the answer when it comes back.

node-runtime.caption: One thread takes every request. The trick is never blocking it: slow work goes to the system and your code handles the answer.
steps: The host is the event loop. Real name: one thread juggling many requests. It takes a request and hands it off without waiting.
A host's quick reply is the callback. Real name: your code runs briefly when an event fires. Keep it short or every guest waits.
The kitchen is non-blocking I/O. Real name: disk and network work happens off the loop in the OS or thread pool.
The dish arriving is the response. Real name: the result comes back as a callback, and the host moves on to the next guest.

analogy.name: Airport security checkpoints
analogy.line: The middleware chain is like airport security: each checkpoint either waves you through to the next or stops you. Boarding (the handler) only sees passengers who passed all of them.

express-nest.caption: Express runs middleware in registration order. Each one either passes the request on or ends it, and there is no other move.
steps: The passenger arrives at the first checkpoint. Real name: the request enters the chain with nothing decided yet.
A camera that only watches is middleware 1. Real name: logging. It observes, then always calls next().
The ID check is middleware 2. Real name: auth. It may refuse and end the request here without calling next().
Boarding is the handler. Real name: the route code, which only ever sees requests that passed every gate.
The exit path goes back through the chain. Real name: the response flows out, so order matters on the way out too.
